bib.title: LLM in a flash: Efficient Large Language Model Inference with Limited Memory

question: How can an LLM whose weights exceed available DRAM be run efficiently by storing parameters in flash and loading them on demand?
hypothesis: Exploiting FFN activation sparsity with reuse across recent tokens and larger contiguous reads makes flash-resident inference of models up to 2x DRAM size practical.
contributions: Study of flash and DRAM hardware characteristics and an inference cost model (Sec 2)
Techniques: sparsity predictor, windowing, row-column bundling, preallocated DRAM management (Sec 3)
Runs models 2x larger than DRAM with up to 4x, 7x, 20x speedup on CPU, Metal and NVIDIA GPU vs naive (Sec 4)

method.summary: Weights stay in flash. A per-layer low-rank predictor forecasts which FFN neurons fire; only those are read, neurons of the last k tokens are kept in a preallocated DRAM matrix (windowing), and each neuron's up-projection column and down-projection row are stored together (bundling) to double chunk size. Embeddings and attention weights stay in DRAM.

datasets.name: C4 validation subset
datasets.size: small subset (size not stated); 100 random samples for sparsity statistics
datasets.split: first 128 tokens as prompt, 256 tokens generated

datasets.name: refined-web
datasets.split: relufication fine-tuning of Phi-2 (following Mirzadeh et al. 2023)

datasets.name: Arc Easy, Arc Challenge, HellaSwag, MMLU, wikitext2

models.name: Low-rank activation predictor
models.params: OPT: rank 128 (first 28 layers), 1024 (last 4); average rank 240; Falcon: 256/1152; Persimmon: 256/1152; Phi-2: 160/480/800 by layer group; Llama 2: 1024 in 4 middle layers, 256 elsewhere
models.architecture: two-layer low-rank (N to R to M) with sigmoid output, active if > threshold

other.input: output of current layer's attention module
other.threshold: 0.5 default, 0.7 Persimmon, 0.4/0.55 Phi-2 rows in Table 4
other.loss: balanced over negative and positive samples

training.objective: balanced binary loss on per-neuron ReLU activation (predictor); Phi-2 relufication fine-tune with distillation loss
training.compute: 4 hours on an A100 per layer predictor

other.scope: base LLMs are not trained here except Phi-2 relufication; only predictors are trained

inference.decoding: greedy for most runs; nucleus sampling p=0.9 for Persimmon and in Sec 5.1 comparisons; speculative decoding with lambda=4 on GPU
inference.max_tokens: 256 new tokens (1000 in the long-generation ablation)
inference.samples: latency averaged over a small C4 validation subset; standard deviations in Table 5; seeds not stated
inference.prompting: first 128 tokens of each C4 example as prompt

parameters.window_size_k: 5 tokens in Fig 4; k=4 for OPT/Falcon/Persimmon/Phi-2; k=2 for Llama 2
parameters.memory_budget: about 50% of model size (65% for Phi-2; stop caching above 55% for Llama 2; 25% of FFN cap for Persimmon)

other.hardware: Apple M1 Max 1TB SSD (CPU float32; Metal float16), Apple M2 Ultra 2TB SSD (Metal), Linux machine with 24GB RTX 4090 (bfloat16)
other.software: HuggingFace Transformers, PyTorch, MLX Metal kernels, macOS 14.3
other.io: F_NOCACHE on macOS, DirectIO on Linux, purge before benchmarks; I/O latency for baselines is best theoretical number

metrics.name: per-token inference latency
metrics.definition: I/O + memory management + compute, averaged per generated token

metrics.name: zero-shot accuracy (Arc Easy, Arc Challenge, HellaSwag)

baselines: Naive: load whole model on demand each forward pass (at least half the model transferred)
Hybrid: half of model persisted, other half loaded per token, no sparsity
eval.protocol: Single sequence at a time; standard deviations reported in Table 5; no significance test; seeds not stated

evidence.quote: We used best theoretical possible numbers for IO latency for each of the methods to make a fair comparison, the real number might be higher.

results.claim: OPT 6.7B on RTX 4090 GPU: all techniques cut per-token latency from naive loading to 84 ms.
results.setup: OPT 6.7B, bfloat16, RTX 4090 24GB, about half the model in memory, batch 1, 128-token prompt, 256 generated, C4 validation subset; naive I/O is a theoretical best-case number
results.note: 2218/84 is about 26x; abstract says up to 20x and discussion says 20-25x
results.quote: up to 4x and 20x increase in inference speed
results.table: Table 3, rows OPT 6.7B Naive/All, backend GPU, column Total (2218 vs 84)

results.claim: OPT 6.7B on M1 Max CPU: 3182 ms naive to 669 ms (about 4.8x).
results.setup: OPT 6.7B float32, M1 Max CPU, half of model in DRAM, batch 1
results.quote: an acceleration in inference speed of 4-5x compared to traditional loading methods in CPU
results.table: Table 3, rows OPT 6.7B Naive/All, backend CPU, column Total (3182 vs 669)

results.claim: Ablation of I/O latency: predictor, windowing, bundling reduce OPT 6.7B flash I/O latency from 2196 ms to 87 ms.
results.setup: OPT 6.7B 16 bit on M1 Max, half memory available; 13.4 GB read naive at 6.10 GB/s; final config reads 0.2 GB at 2.25 GB/s
results.table: Table 2, last row (Hybrid+Predictor+Windowing+Bundling), column I/O Latency; first row 2196

results.claim: Bundling roughly doubles sparse-read throughput (1.25 to 2.25 GB/s) and halves I/O latency (164 to 87 ms).
results.setup: OPT 6.7B 16 bit, M1 Max, windowing on
results.table: Table 2, rows Windowing without/with Bundling, column I/O Latency (164 vs 87)

results.claim: Sparse scattered reads give lower throughput than a dense linear read (1.25 vs 6.1 GiB/s), yet the overall effect stays strongly favourable.
results.setup: OPT 6.7B on M1 Max, without bundling
results.quote: e.g. 1.25 GiB/s sparse vs 6.1 GiB/s dense

results.claim: Metal M2 Ultra speedup is 7.4x (2270 to 305 ms).
results.setup: OPT 6.7B float16, Apple M2 Ultra, Metal
results.note: Naive Metal M2 I/O is 2145 ms, not 2196
results.table: Table 3, rows OPT 6.7B Naive/All, backend Metal M2 (2270 vs 305)

results.claim: Other models, CPU totals (naive to All): Falcon 7B 3095 to 706, Persimmon 8B 3806 to 1041, Phi-2 2.7B 1287 to 546, Llama 2 7B 3095 to 994.
results.setup: M1 Max CPU, float32, about 50% of model in memory (65% for Phi-2); Hybrid baseline loads half the model per token without sparsity
results.note: Llama 2 uses window 2 and a FATReLU-sparsified model; text says 3x for Llama 2 and 2.35x for Phi-2
results.table: Table 3, rows Llama 2 7B Naive/All, column Total (3095 vs 994); Falcon 3095 vs 706

results.claim: Speculative decoding on the GPU lowers OPT 6.7B latency to 60 ms per token, a 1.4x gain.
results.note: Text says 'as shown in table 5'; the numbers are in Tables 3 and 5. Original speculative decoding speedup quoted as 1.58x
results.quote: improve the speed of decoding by 1.4x
results.table: Table 3, row OPT 6.7B Speculative GPU, column Total (60)

results.claim: Low-rank predictors barely change zero-shot accuracy on OPT 6.7B.
results.setup: OPT 6.7B, ranks 1024 (last 4 layers) and 128 elsewhere, threshold 0.5; Arc Easy 66.1 to 66.2, Arc Challenge 30.6 to 30.6, HellaSwag 50.3 to 49.8
results.quote: using predictors does not adversely affect the model’s performance in 0-shot tasks
results.table: Table 4, row OPT 6.7B with predictors, column HellaSwag

results.claim: Accuracy cost is larger for non-ReLU models: relufied Falcon 7B with predictors loses 1.4 to 4.0 points vs relufied-only on HellaSwag depending on predictor rank; Phi-2 MMLU drops from 57 to 54.3 after relufication and to about 52 with predictors.
results.setup: Falcon 7B relufied HellaSwag 54.17, with predictors 50.74 to 53.16; Phi-2 MMLU via InstructEval
results.quote: MMLU metric drops from 57 to 54.3 after relufication with distillation
results.table: Table 4, Falcon 7B relufied rows, column HellaSwag; App C.4 text

results.claim: Llama 2 7B MMLU: 41.8 original, 38.96 FATReLU-sparsified, 38.63 with predictors.
Windowing cuts OPT 6.7B fresh FFN loading from about 10% of DRAM capacity (predictor alone) to 2.4%, at a total DRAM use of 52.1% of model size.
results.setup: OPT 6.7B, window k=4 (past 5 tokens held), predictors ranks 128/1024
results.quote: with our method, it drops to 2.4%

results.claim: OPT 6.7B predictors average 5% false negatives and 7% false positives.
results.quote: an average of 5% false negatives and 7% false positives

results.claim: Predictors take about 2.75% of inference time on M1 Max CPU and 4.8% on RTX GPU for OPT 6.7B.
results.quote: this was comprising 2.75% and in RTX GPU it was 4.8% of inference time

results.claim: Sparse model uses lower power but more total energy than a dense model, because generation takes longer.
results.quote: the sparse model having a higher total energy consumption

results.claim: Bundling neurons by co-activation (closest friend) failed: highly active neurons are the closest friend of many, so they were loaded repeatedly.
results.setup: OPT 6.7B, C4 validation co-activation statistics; closest friend coactivates at least 95% of the time
results.quote: bundling worked against our original intention

results.claim: Latency does not grow with generation length up to 1000 tokens and nucleus sampling does not hurt the method.
results.setup: OPT 6.7B on GPU and CPU, greedy and nucleus
results.quote: the average flash latency doesn’t increase as we go further in generation

results.claim: Flash random-read throughput exceeds 6 GiB/s only for large linear reads; 32 KiB or larger random reads over multiple threads suffice for sparse inference.
results.setup: MacBook M1 Max 1TB flash, uncached 1GiB linear read
results.quote: speeds exceeding 6 GiB/s for a 1GiB linear read of an uncached file

limits: Single-batch decoding only; prompt processing and multi-batch not studied (Sec 8)
Requires sparse (ReLU-like) FFN activations; Falcon, Phi-2 and Llama 2 needed relufication or FATReLU fine-tuning, which costs accuracy
Memory fixed at about half the model size; other sizes left to future work
Baseline I/O latencies are theoretical best case, not measured
Total energy is higher than dense despite lower power; no quantitative power or thermal analysis
Latency sampled from a small C4 subset; no seeds stated; code and weights not released in the text
Predictors over-predict: about 3x the truly active neurons are loaded in OPT and Persimmon

terms.definition: keep in DRAM the neurons predicted active for the last k tokens and load only the incremental difference
store the i-th up-projection column and i-th down-projection row together to double the read chunk

lineage.note: low-rank activation predictor; this paper uses current-layer attention output as input
